decisions.rationale: A completion that fails the pending or duplicate checks is still passed to domain_replay_step; even a rejected step is then recorded as completed and removed from pending. This changes the state used to assess later entries and can produce cascading incorrect findings.
The idempotency key is only path-validated. Effect status, guards, and writes remain keyed exclusively by correlation, so the declared idempotency key has no deduplication effect.

The source is read and validated while constructing the migration plan, but the later write path checks only that the destination is currently a regular file. It never verifies that the destination still contains the source used to compute the replacement, so an intervening edit can be silently overwritten.

A new request is forbidden only while Pending or after Succeeded. From Failed or TimedOut the command can set Pending and reset attempts to one, bypassing the retry action's maximum-attempt guard indefinitely.

The checker returns nonzero for signature-invalid, but the supplied excerpts omit the evaluation helper's possible remaining statuses and their required exit semantics. A missing transition cannot be established reliably.

Pending and completed keys preserve stringified correlation identifiers, but the corresponding state-machine parameter is coerced to i64 and every nonnumeric value becomes 0. Distinct identifiers can therefore drive the same correlation state while remaining distinct lifecycle keys, producing inconsistent pending and duplicate decisions.
Locations and tags alone do not establish a check/write gap or an inconsistent cross-file contract.
Materially identical to adj:sha256:0377f387beeea87cc36e0ec9e6f333dca53a1cc278849db49fda7bb571826e17: both track correlation identifiers through incompatible string bookkeeping and integer coercion.

The temporary path uses only the source stem and process ID, and std::fs::write replaces an existing path. Two live materializations of the same input in one process therefore share a file, so one can overwrite or remove the file still used by the other; a pre-existing same-name path is also overwritten.

Creation reads and validates the target, then persists a record referring to its mutable path without ensuring the file still contains those bytes. A target change during that interval can make a successfully created record immediately inconsistent.
The supplied locations and tags do not show the relevant checks, writes, or key stability, so the allegation cannot be reliably assessed.

Named domains and inline TypeExpr ranges are constructed without checking lo <= hi. The same inverted bounds used by static liveness binding enumeration silently produce no bindings, so an empty range is accepted instead of rejected.
i64::div_euclid and rem_euclid overflow for i64::MIN with -1. Unlike addition, subtraction, and multiplication, these paths are unchecked and can panic instead of returning RuntimeError.

The check path validates only the approval target kind before rendering supplied approvals. It never binds their specification, claim-set, target, or reviewed digests to the current inputs, so stale or unrelated approvals can be incorporated into an expected document and accepted as conformant.
